title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Painting
audience: Painters and painting contractors, including solo operators, who write quotes for interior and exterior repaints and want to justify a higher price on value.
learningOutcomes: Write a painting offer with a clear finish, a time frame, the client's tasks and a guarantee
Identify the friction and risk a homeowner or landlord carries and reduce them
Price a repaint on value and cost, not only on hours

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will paint your house' is a service. 'I will repaint the three bedrooms and the hallway in the two colours you approve, finished in four working days, with a preparation checklist, photos at sign-off and a touch-up visit' is an offer. The client is buying rooms they can move back into, and the certainty that the walls will look right when the furniture returns.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: State the outcome: the rooms, the approved colours and the finish. Set a time frame in working days. List what the client must do, such as clearing furniture, confirming colours and giving access. Add one certainty element, such as a preparation checklist, photos or a walk-through at sign-off. Name the risk you carry, such as a touch-up visit within a stated period. Put the scope and exclusions in writing, for example ceilings not included, timber repairs excluded, or wallpaper removal extra, because a written quote becomes binding once accepted (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes, last updated 1 August 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction
instruction.body: Make the booking, colour choice, access and handover simple. A colour-selection sheet, a fixed start day, a key-handover routine and a clean end-of-day tidy-up each remove a decision or a worry for the client. Fewer steps and fewer decisions for the client usually support a higher price, because the client pays for certainty and for less disruption, not only for paint on the wall.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and workmanship
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. Consumer guarantees under the Australian Consumer Law apply to services and cannot be excluded by contract, and a 'no refunds' line does not override a customer's rights for services (business.gov.au, Warranties and refunds, last updated 27 May 2025). A written workmanship warranty is an optional promise that sits on top of those guarantees. In Victoria, a business is generally given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault at no charge (Consumer Victoria, Services not done with due care and skill, last updated 13 October 2023). That page does not set a fix-window length, so choose your own window and check its cost before you publish it.

instruction.heading: Pricing on value
instruction.body: Price from the finish and the risk, then check the price against cost and time. A higher price is easier to defend when the client can see the preparation, the finish standard and the saved disruption. Government guidance says a quote should recover every cost and add a margin, so check the price against cost before adding any premium (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes). Stepped packages, for example walls only, walls and ceilings, or a full interior with trim and a touch-up visit, let the client see what each step adds (Jobber Academy, Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024). That source is an older, general service article and not painting data. Show one clear total and say whether GST is included, as WA Consumer Protection asks for WA quotes (updated 4 September 2026).

procedure: Write the finished result for the rooms or the building in one sentence a client would repeat.
Set a time frame in working days, and record how often past jobs met it, including drying time between coats.
List what the client must do, such as clearing furniture, approving colours and confirming access, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element, such as a preparation checklist, photos or a sign-off walk-through.
Decide the touch-up or guarantee terms, and check that you can afford them.
Price from value, then check the rate against cost and time.

workedExamples.situation: A painter quotes an hourly rate for a three-bedroom interior and loses jobs to lower quotes. Clients say they cannot tell what the finished walls will look like or how long the house will be disrupted.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer and decide how to price it.
workedExamples.reasoning: A fixed-scope package with a colour sheet, a preparation checklist, photos at sign-off and a touch-up visit gives the client certainty that an hourly quote does not. The painter then checks the package price against cost and time. A vendor listing gives a range of $3,500 to $8,000 for a full three-bedroom interior (TradeRefer painting page, undated, vendor listing, not market data). Use that range only as a sense-check. The package price has to come from the painter's own costs and hours, and any premium must be explained by what the package delivers.

commonErrors.error: Making a guarantee you cannot afford to honour
commonErrors.prevention: Limit the guarantee to something you control, such as a touch-up visit within a stated period, and cost that visit before you publish it.

commonErrors.error: Stating a result you cannot substantiate, such as a longer-lasting finish with no test behind it
commonErrors.prevention: Use only results you have measured or can show, and get the client's consent before using their photos.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Painting work can need a licence or registration in some states, and the job value can decide it. In NSW, a contractor licence is needed for residential building work valued at more than $5,000 in labour and materials including GST. Check the rules for the state where the work is done before you quote.
Pricing statements are covered by the Australian Consumer Law. The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited (ACCC, Setting prices: what's allowed, last modified 15 July 2026).

qualityStandard: Every painting offer is written down, with scope, exclusions, client tasks and the guarantee terms.
Offer and pricing decisions are checked against cost and time, and against the licence rule for the job value in the state where the work is done.
documentationEvidence: Written painting offer with scope, exclusions and touch-up terms
Dated cost and time check for the price
Evidence collected, such as photos of past finishes with the client's consent, and the decision made
summary: A painting offer promises a finished result, a time frame, certainty and a fair guarantee.
A higher rate follows from clearer value, such as preparation and less disruption, not from longer hours.
Check the state licence rule for the job value before you publish a price.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a painting offer does the client buy?
options: Your hourly rate and your ute
Your equipment list and the brand of paint you carry
How many years you have been painting

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a painting guarantee or touch-up promise be?
options: Unlimited, with no end date and no defined scope
Something you can deliver and afford
Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends

knowledgeChecks.question: What must a measurable claim about a finish, such as a stated longer life, have?

officialReferences.title: Prepare quotes (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: Says a written quote becomes binding once accepted and that a quote should recover cost plus a margin. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.

officialReferences.title: Warranties and refunds (business.gov.au)
officialReferences.covers: Says an optional warranty sits on top of consumer guarantees, and that a no-refunds line does not override service rights. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.

officialReferences.title: Setting prices: what's allowed (ACCC)
officialReferences.covers: States that misleading price statements are prohibited. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.

officialReferences.title: Estimates, quotes and deposits (WA Consumer Protection)
officialReferences.covers: Western Australia only. Supports showing one total and whether GST is included, getting written approval before extra work, and a deposit generally no more than 10 per cent. Read in the SOL-03 tactics research on 2026-11-09.

sourceReferences: Consumer Victoria, 'Services not done with due care and skill', https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/products-and-services/problem-with-a-service/services-not-done-with-due-care-and-skill, last updated 13 October 2023. Supports: a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge; no fix-window length given.

Business Queensland, 'Preparing a business quote: tips', https://www.business.qld.gov.au/running-business/marketing-sales/sales/preparing-quote/tips, last updated 16 November 2022. Supports: add-ons shown as separate lines on the quote; follow-up 7 to 14 days after quoting.

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Older general service source; supports stepped packages.

INSEAD Knowledge, 'Small Change, Big Rewards', https://knowledge.insead.edu/marketing/small-change-big-rewards, 2 October 2025. Not a trade study; supports the idea that the order in which plans are shown can change which plan buyers choose. Figure not used.

LifestyleTradie, 'Hourly Rate or Flat Rate', https://www.lifestyletradie.com.au/?p=12927, published 21 February 2022, last modified 28 April 2023. Opinion and anecdote; supports a mix of flat pricing for predictable work and time-based pricing for uncertain work.
